done.why: I'd seen every room I could reach. The paths left were a well bucket that wouldn't go up, a ledge the game said I wasn't ready for, two rockfalls that said 'will have to wait', and a unicorn I'd scared off. Nothing I had seemed to open any of them, and getting through the random carousel again and again had worn me down.

about: An old barrow leads down into a cavern full of ruins: a fancy underground garden with a unicorn wearing a gold key, topiary that moves when you aren't looking, a spinning room that sends you somewhere random, and a stone door that only opens if you answer a riddle. A little wizard pops in and out. It feels like the start of something bigger that I'm not allowed into yet. Several ways on are blocked, with messages saying they'll keep until later.

moments.note: My sword started glowing near the unicorn. A nice warning that something was around.
The topiary animals had moved a little. Creepy, in a good way.
The rockfall message 'Whatever lies beyond it will have to wait' felt like the game telling me where its edge was.
I answered 'a well' and only got a hollow laugh. 'say well' worked. Same answer, different wording.
A clap of thunder and the stone door swung open. Solving the riddle felt good.
The etchings were broken letters, 'o b o / A G I / E L / m p a'. I couldn't make anything of them.
The wizard showed up, muttered into his beard and vanished.
When I grabbed for the key, the unicorn decided I was an 'uncouth sort of vagabond' and left. It was funny even though I'd blown it.
It took about 20 tries in the random carousel to get back to the Riddle Room. Tedious.
The bucket is tied to the well, and getting in does nothing. I had no water and nothing to carry it in.

wished: Get the key off the unicorn some gentler way, maybe by befriending it or offering it something
Fill something with water at the ford and use it to make the bucket rise
Find something inside the gazebo, which looked like it ought to hold things
Walk out of the carousel in the direction I chose, or find a way to stop it spinning
Climb up to the ledge at the Deep Ford

lines.line: The passage south is choked with a fall of rock not far in. Whatever lies beyond it will have to wait.
lines.why: It told me plainly that part of this place was shut off for now.

lines.line: You start up toward the ledge, and the rock comes away in your hand. Whatever is along there will keep until you are better equipped for it.
lines.why: It hinted that I'd need some piece of gear first, so I went looking for one.

lines.line: What is tall as a house, round as a cup, and all the king's horses can't draw it up?
lines.why: The one clear puzzle I solved.

lines.line: The unicorn, unsurprised by this evidence that you are indeed the uncouth sort of vagabond it suspected you were, melts into the hedges and is gone.
lines.why: Funny and in character. It also lost me the key.

lines.line: The bucket is far too large to carry, and it is tied to the well.
lines.why: It told me this was a well I could ride up, but not how to make it go.

fun.why: The riddle door and the unicorn moments were fun. Too much of the game, though, was spent fighting the random carousel to get back where I'd been.

engagement.why: I had a goal at first, getting the key and getting up the well. Once every lead ended at a wall I couldn't get through, I lost momentum.

difficulty.why: The riddle was fair, apart from how picky it was about wording. I had no way at all to get the bucket moving or to get the key, and the carousel made every trip back slow.

interestingness.why: Shifting topiary, a glowing sword, a wizard who drops in, a riddle door and a well bucket. Lots of good ideas in a small space.

prose.why: Clear and atmospheric, with some dry wit (the unicorn, the gazebo as 'the sort of thing one takes tea in').
